children.text: pratītyajānāṃ bhāvānāṃ naiḥsvābhāvyaṃ jagāda yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who declared the essencelessness (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>) of things that arise dependently (<s>pratītyaja</s>),

children.text: taṃ namāmy asamajñānam acintyam anidarśanam || NagAst_01
children.translated_text: I bow to that incomparable knowledge (<s>asamajñāna</s>), inconceivable and beyond demonstration. || 1 ||

children.text: yathā tvayā mahāyāne dharmanairātmyam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: Just as by you in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) was by yourself

children.text: viditaṃ deśitaṃ tadvad dhīmadbhyaḥ karuṇāvaśāt || NagAst_02
children.translated_text: understood and taught to the wise, out of the power of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). || 2 ||

children.text: pratyayebhyaḥ samutpannam anutpannaṃ tvayoditam |
children.translated_text: What has arisen from conditions, you declared as unarisen;

children.text: svabhāvena na taj jātam iti śūnyaṃ prakāśitam || NagAst_03
children.translated_text: it is not born by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — thus emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) was revealed. || 3 ||

children.text: yadvac chabdaṃ pratītyeha pratiśabdasamudbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as an echo arises here in dependence on a sound,

children.text: māyāmarīcivac cāpi tathā bhavasamudbhavaḥ || NagAst_04
children.translated_text: and just like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) or a mirage (<s>marīci</s>), so too is the arising of existence (<s>bhava</s>). || 4 ||

children.text: māyāmarīcigandharvanagarapratibimbakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Illusions, mirages, <s>gandharva</s>-cities, and reflections —

children.text: yady ajātāḥ saha svapnair na syāt taddarśanādikam || NagAst_05
children.translated_text: if they, along with dreams, are unborn, then there would be no seeing of them and so forth. || 5 ||

children.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtā yathaite kṛtakāḥ smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as these, born from causes and conditions, are considered created (<s>kṛtaka</s>),

children.text: tadvat pratyayajaṃ viśvaṃ tvayoktaṃ nātha sāṃvṛtam || NagAst_06
children.translated_text: so too, O Lord, the universe born from conditions has been declared by you as conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>). || 6 ||

children.text: asty etat kṛtakaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiṃcid bālalāpanam |
children.translated_text: Whatever childish babbling says 'all this exists and is created' —

children.text: riktamuṣṭipratīkāśam ayathārthaprakāśitam || NagAst_07
children.translated_text: it is like [the trick of] an empty fist, revealed as not in accordance with reality. || 7 ||

children.text: kṛtakaṃ vastu no jātaṃ tadā kiṃ vārtamānikam |
children.translated_text: If a created thing is not [truly] born, then how can it be present?

children.text: kasya nāśād atītaṃ syād utpitsuḥ kim apekṣate || NagAst_08
children.translated_text: From whose destruction would it be past? What does that which is about to arise depend upon? || 8 ||

children.text: svasmān na jāyate bhāvaḥ parasmān nobhayād api |
children.translated_text: A thing does not arise from itself, nor from another, nor from both;

children.text: na san nāsan na sadasan kutaḥ kasyodayas tadā || NagAst_09
children.translated_text: neither from the existent, nor the non-existent, nor both — then whence the arising of what? || 9 ||

children.text: ajāte na svabhāvo 'sti kutaḥ svasmāt samudbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: In what is unborn, there is no own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — whence then arising from itself?

children.text: svabhāvābhāvasiddhyaiva parasmād apy asaṃbhavah || NagAst_10
children.translated_text: By the very establishment of the absence of own-nature, arising from another too is impossible. || 10 ||

children.text: svatve sati paratvaṃ syāt paratve svatvam iṣyate |
children.translated_text: When there is selfhood, there can be otherness; when there is otherness, selfhood is accepted;

children.text: āpekṣikī tayoḥ siddhiḥ pārāvāram ivoditā || NagAst_11
children.translated_text: the establishment of both is declared to be mutually dependent, like the hither and farther shore. || 11 ||

children.text: yadā nāpekṣate kiṃ cit kutaḥ kiṃ cit tadā bhavet |
children.translated_text: When [a thing] does not depend on anything, how can anything then exist?

children.text: yadā nāpekṣate dīrghaṃ kuto hrasvādikaṃ tadā || NagAst_12
children.translated_text: When the long does not depend [on the short], whence then the short and the like? || 12 ||

children.text: astitve sati nāstitvaṃ dīrghe hrasvaṃ tathā sati |
children.translated_text: When existence obtains, there is non-existence; when the long obtains, there is the short;

children.text: nāstitve sati cāstitvaṃ yat tasmād ubhayaṃ na sat || NagAst_13
children.translated_text: when non-existence obtains, there is existence — therefore both are unreal. || 13 ||

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca tathānekam atītānāgatādi ca |
children.translated_text: Unity and likewise multiplicity, past and future and so on,

children.text: saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca samyaṅmithyā svataḥ kutaḥ || NagAst_14
children.translated_text: defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>), right and wrong — whence [do they arise] from themselves? || 14 ||

children.text: svata eva hi yo nāsti bhāvaḥ sarvo 'sti kas tadā |
children.translated_text: For when a thing does not exist from itself, what 'everything exists' [means] then?

children.text: para ity ucyate yo 'yaṃ na vinā svasvabhāvataḥ || NagAst_15
children.translated_text: This which is called 'other' — [it too] does not [exist] apart from its own nature. || 15 ||

children.text: na svabhāvo 'sti bhāvānāṃ parabhāvo 'sti no yadā |
children.translated_text: When there is no own-nature of things, and no other-nature either,

children.text: bhāvagrahagrahāveśaḥ paratantro 'sti kas tadā || NagAst_16
children.translated_text: what then is this dependent possession (<s>paratantra</s>) by the seizing of the grasping of things' existence? || 16 ||

children.text: ādāv eva samaṃ jātāḥ svabhāvena ca nirvṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: From the very beginning equally arisen, and by [their own] nature fully passed away (<s>nirvṛta</s>),

children.text: anutpannāś ca tattvena tasmād dharmās tvayoditāḥ || NagAst_17
children.translated_text: and truly unborn — thus have <s>dharmas</s> been declared by you. || 17 ||

children.text: niḥsvabhāvās tvayā dhīman rūpādyāḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: O wise one, form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the rest have been revealed by you as without own-nature,

children.text: phenabudbudamāyābhramarīcikadalīsamāḥ || NagAst_18
children.translated_text: comparable to foam, bubbles, illusion (<s>māyā</s>), clouds, mirages, and plantain trunks. || 18 ||

children.text: indriyair upalabdhaṃ yat tat tattvena bhaved yadi |
children.translated_text: If what is perceived by the sense-organs were real in truth,

children.text: jātās tattvavido bālās tattvajñānena kiṃ tadā || NagAst_19
children.translated_text: then the childish would be knowers of reality — what then [would be the need for] knowledge of truth? || 19 ||

children.text: jaḍatvam apramāṇatvam athāvyākṛtatām api |
children.translated_text: Inertness (<s>jaḍatva</s>), unreliability (<s>apramāṇatva</s>), indeterminacy (<s>avyākṛtatā</s>),

children.text: viparītaparijñānam indriyānāṃ tvam ūcivān || NagAst_20
children.translated_text: and distorted comprehension — you declared [these to be the nature] of the sense-organs. || 20 ||

children.text: ajñānenāvṛto yena yathāvan na prapadyate |
children.translated_text: The world, covered by ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), does not comprehend [things] as they really are;

children.text: lokas tena yathābhūtam iti matvā tvayoditam || NagAst_21
children.translated_text: having understood that, 'as things really are' (<s>yathābhūtam</s>) was taught by you. || 21 ||

children.text: astīti śāśvatī dṛṣtir nāstīty ucchedadarśanam |
children.translated_text: 'It exists' is the eternalist view (<s>śāśvatadṛṣṭi</s>); 'It does not exist' is the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadarśana</s>);

children.text: tenāntadvayanirmukto dharmo 'yaṃ deśitas tvayā || NagAst_22
children.translated_text: therefore, free from both extremes (<s>antadvaya</s>), this <s>Dharma</s> was taught by you. || 22 ||

children.text: catuṣkoṭivinirmuktās tena dharmās tvayoditāḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>dharmas</s>, free from the four alternatives (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>), have been declared by you,

children.text: vijñānasyāpy avijñeyā vācāṃ kim uta gocarāḥ || NagAst_23
children.translated_text: not objects even of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — how much less the domain of words. || 23 ||

children.text: svapnendrajālikodbhūtaṃ dvicandrodvīkṣaṇaṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: Just as seeing a double moon, produced by a dream or a magician's illusion (<s>indrajālika</s>) —

children.text: bhūtaṃ tadvastu no bhūtaṃ tathā dṛṣṭaṃ jagat tvayā || NagAst_24
children.translated_text: that thing is seen but does not truly exist — so has the world been seen by you. || 24 ||

children.text: utpannaś ca sthito naṣṭaḥ svapne yadvat sutas tathā |
children.translated_text: Just as a son is born, exists, and dies in a dream,

children.text: na cotpannaḥ sthito naṣṭa ukto loko 'rthatas tvayā || NagAst_25
children.translated_text: yet is neither born, nor has existed, nor has died — so has the world been declared by you in its true meaning. || 25 ||

children.text: kāraṇāt saṃbhavo dṛṣṭo yathā svapne tathetaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as arising from a cause is seen in a dream, so too in the other [waking state];

children.text: saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ vibhavo 'pi matas tathā || NagAst_26
children.translated_text: the arising of all things, and dissolution too, is considered likewise. || 26 ||

children.text: rāgādijaṃ yathā duḥkhaṃ saṃkleśasaṃsṛtī tathā |
children.translated_text: Just as suffering born from passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, and defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and transmigration (<s>saṃsṛti</s>),

children.text: saṃbhārapūraṇān muktiḥ svapnavad bhāṣitā tvayā || NagAst_27
children.translated_text: [so too] liberation (<s>mukti</s>) through the fulfillment of the accumulations [of merit and wisdom] (<s>saṃbhāra</s>) has been declared by you as like a dream. || 27 ||

children.text: jātaṃ tathaiva no jātam āgataṃ gatam ity api |
children.translated_text: 'Born' and likewise 'not born,' 'arrived' and likewise 'departed,'

children.text: baddho muktas tathā jñānī dvayam icchen na tattvavit || NagAst_28
children.translated_text: 'bound' and likewise 'a knower liberated' — one who knows the truth does not desire [either member of] the pair. || 28 ||

children.text: utpattir yasya naivāsti tasya kā nirvṛtir bhavet |
children.translated_text: For that which has no arising whatsoever, what cessation could there be?

children.text: māyāgajaprakāśatvād ādiśāntatvam arthataḥ || NagAst_29
children.translated_text: Because of being like the appearance of a magical elephant, it is primordially quiescent in reality. (verse 29)

children.text: utpanno 'pi na cotpanno yadvan māyāgajo mataḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a magical elephant, even though appearing, is considered not arisen,

children.text: utpannaṃ ca tathā viśvam anutpannaṃ ca tattvataḥ || NagAst_30
children.translated_text: so too the entire universe, though arisen, is unarisen in reality. (verse 30)

children.text: ameyair aprameyānāṃ pratyekaṃ nirvṛtiḥ kṛtā |
children.translated_text: By immeasurable Lords of the World, the <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation) of immeasurable beings was brought about individually,

children.text: lokanāthair hi sattvānāṃ na kaś cin mocitaś ca taiḥ || NagAst_31
children.translated_text: yet not a single being was liberated by them. (verse 31)

children.text: te ca sattvāś ca no jātā ye nirvānti na te sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: Those beings were never born, and those who attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> clearly do not exist;

children.text: na kaś cin mocitaḥ kaiś cid iti proktaṃ mahāmune || NagAst_32
children.translated_text: "No one was liberated by anyone" — thus You have declared, O Great Sage. (verse 32)

children.text: māyākārakṛtaṃ yadvad vastuśūnyaṃ tathetarat |
children.translated_text: Just as what is created by a magician is empty of substance, so too is everything else;

children.text: vastuśūnyaṃ jagat sarvaṃ tvayoktaṃ kārakas tathā || NagAst_33
children.translated_text: the entire world is empty of substance — thus You have declared — and so too is the doer. (verse 33)

children.text: kārako 'pi kṛto 'nyena kṛtatvaṃ nātivartate |
children.translated_text: The doer too is made by another and does not transcend being made;

children.text: atha vā tatkriyākartṛ kārakasya prasajyate || NagAst_34
children.translated_text: or else, the doership of that action would apply to the doer himself. (verse 34)

children.text: nāmamātraṃ jagat sarvam ity uccair bhāṣitaṃ tvayā |
children.translated_text: "The entire world is nothing but names" — thus You have loudly proclaimed;

children.text: abhidhānāt pṛthagbhūtam abhidheyaṃ na vidyate || NagAst_35
children.translated_text: the signified, being separate from the signifier, does not exist. (verse 35)

children.text: kalpanāmātram ity asmāt sarvadharmāḥ prakāśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) have been shown to be mere conceptual construction;

children.text: kalpanāpy asatī proktā yayā śūnyaṃ vikalpyate || NagAst_36
children.translated_text: and even that conceptual construction is declared to be non-existent — that by which <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is conceived. (verse 36)

children.text: bhāvābhāvadvayātītam anatītaṃ ca kutra cit |
children.translated_text: That which has gone beyond the duality of existence and non-existence, yet has not gone beyond anywhere,

children.text: na ca jñānaṃ na ca jñeyaṃ na cāsti na ca nāsti yat || NagAst_37
children.translated_text: which is neither knowledge nor the knowable, which neither exists nor does not exist, (verse 37)

children.text: yan na caikaṃ na cānekaṃ nobhayaṃ na ca nobhayam |
children.translated_text: which is neither one nor many, neither both nor neither,

children.text: anālayam athāvyaktam acintyam anidarśanam || NagAst_38
children.translated_text: without foundation, unmanifest, inconceivable, without indication — (verse 38)

children.text: yan nodeti na ca vyeti nocchedi na ca śāśvatam |
children.translated_text: which neither arises nor ceases, is neither annihilated nor eternal,

children.text: tad ākāśapratīkāśaṃ nākṣarajñānagocaram || NagAst_39
children.translated_text: that, resembling space, is not the domain of letter-based knowledge. (verse 39)

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatā saiva te matā |
children.translated_text: What is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent co-arising), that itself is considered by You as <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness);

children.text: tathāvidhaś ca saddharmas tatsamaś ca tathāgataḥ || NagAst_40
children.translated_text: and the true <s>Dharma</s> is of that very nature, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> is equal to that. (verse 40)

children.text: tat tattvaṃ paramārtho 'pi tathatā dravyam iṣyate |
children.translated_text: That is the reality, the ultimate truth, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and is regarded as substance;

children.text: bhūtaṃ tad avisaṃvādi tadbodhād buddha ucyate || NagAst_41
children.translated_text: that is the real, the non-deceptive — from the awakening to that, one is called <s>Buddha</s>. (verse 41)

children.text: buddhānāṃ sattvadhātoś ca tenābhinnatvam arthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Buddhas</s> and the realm of beings are in reality non-different;

children.text: ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca samatā tena te matā || NagAst_42
children.translated_text: hence, the equality of self and others is regarded by You. (verse 42)

children.text: bhāvebhyaḥ śūnyatā nānyā na ca bhāvo 'sti tāṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not other than entities, nor does an entity exist without it;

children.text: tasmāt pratītyajā bhāvās tvayā śūnyāḥ prakāśitāḥ || NagAst_43
children.translated_text: therefore, entities that are dependently arisen have been shown by You as empty. (verse 43)

children.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtā paratantrā ca saṃvṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Arisen from causes and conditions, the conventional is dependent on another;

children.text: paratantra iti proktaḥ paramārthas tv akṛtrimaḥ || NagAst_44
children.translated_text: that which is called dependent on another is declared — but the ultimate is uncreated. (verse 44)

children.text: svabhāvaḥ prakṛtis tattvaṃ dravyaṃ vastu sad ity api |
children.translated_text: Own-nature, essential nature, reality, substance, thing, and also being —

children.text: nāsti vai kapito bhāvo paratantras tu vidyate || NagAst_45
children.translated_text: there is indeed no imagined entity; but the dependent does exist. (verse 45)

children.text: astīti kalpite bhāve samāropas tvayoditaḥ |
children.translated_text: In saying "it exists" with regard to an imagined entity, superimposition is taught by You;

children.text: nāstīti kṛtakocchedād ucchedaś ca prakāśitaḥ || NagAst_46
children.translated_text: in saying "it does not exist" due to the destruction of what is produced, annihilation is also shown. (verse 46)

children.text: tattvajñānena nocchedo na ca śāśvatatā matā |
children.translated_text: Through knowledge of reality, neither annihilation nor eternalism is held;

children.text: vastuśūnyaṃ jagat sarvaṃ marīcipratimaṃ matam || NagAst_47
children.translated_text: the entire world, empty of substance, is regarded as comparable to a mirage. (verse 47)

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇājalaṃ yadvan nocchedi na ca śāśvatam |
children.translated_text: Just as the water of a mirage is neither annihilated nor eternal,

children.text: tadvat sarvaṃ jagat proktaṃ nocchedi na ca śāśvatam || NagAst_48
children.translated_text: so too the entire world is declared to be neither annihilated nor eternal. (verse 48)

children.text: dravyam utpadyate yasya tasyocchedādikaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: For one whose substance arises, there would be annihilation and the rest;

children.text: antavān nāntavāṃś cāpi lokas tasya prasajyate || NagAst_49
children.translated_text: for such a one, the world would be both finite and infinite. (verse 49)

children.text: jñāne sati yathā jñeyaṃ jñeye jñānaṃ tathā sati |
children.translated_text: Just as when knowledge exists, there is the knowable, and when the knowable exists, there is knowledge,

children.text: yatrobhayam anutpannam iti buddhaṃ tadāsti kim || NagAst_50
children.translated_text: where both are unarisen — when that is <s>Buddha</s>, then does anything exist? (verse 50)

children.text: iti māyādidṛṣtāntaiḥ sphuṭam uktvā bhiṣagvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, having clearly spoken through examples of illusion and the like, the Supreme Physician

children.text: deśayām āsa saddharmaṃ sarvadṛṣṭicikitsakam || NagAst_51
children.translated_text: taught the true <s>Dharma</s>, which is the remedy for all views. (verse 51)

children.text: etat tat paramaṃ tattvaṃ niḥsvabhāvārthadeśanā |
children.translated_text: This is that supreme reality — the teaching of the meaning of non-self-nature;

children.text: bhāvagrahagṛhītānāṃ cikitseyam anuttarā || NagAst_52
children.translated_text: this is the unsurpassed remedy for those seized by the disease of grasping at entities. (verse 52)

children.text: dharmayājñika tenaiva dharmayajño niruttaraḥ |
children.translated_text: O Sacrificer of the <s>Dharma</s>, by You the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice

children.text: abhīkṣṇam iṣṭas trailokye niṣkapāṭo nirargalaḥ || NagAst_53
children.translated_text: has been continuously offered in the three worlds, without deceit, without obstruction. (verse 53)

children.text: vastugrāhabhayocchedī kutīrthyamṛgabhīkaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Destroying the terror of grasping at substances, terrifying the wild beasts of the heretics —

children.text: nairātmyasiṃhanādo 'yam adbhuto naditas tvayā || NagAst_54
children.translated_text: this wondrous lion's roar of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) has been roared by You. (verse 54)

children.text: śūnyatādharmagambhīrā dharmabherī parāhatā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s>-drum, profound in the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), has been struck;

children.text: naiḥsvābhāvyamahānādo dharmaśaṅkhaḥ prapūritaḥ || NagAst_55
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>-conch, with the great sound of <s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s> (absence of self-nature), has been blown. (verse 55)

children.text: dharmayautukam ākhyātaṃ buddhānāṃ śāsanāmṛtam |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s>-gift has been proclaimed — the nectar of the <s>Buddhas'</s> teaching;

children.text: nītārtham iti nirdiṣṭaṃ dharmāṇāṃ śūnyataiva hi || NagAst_56
children.translated_text: it is designated as of definitive meaning — for the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is indeed that. (verse 56)

children.text: yā tūtpādanirodhādisattvajīvādideśanā |
children.translated_text: But the teaching of arising, cessation, and the like, and of being, living soul, and the like —

children.text: neyārthā ca tvayā nātha bhāṣitā saṃvṛtiś ca sā || NagAst_57
children.translated_text: that was spoken by you, O Lord, as being of provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>), and that is conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). || 57 ||

children.text: prajñāpāramitāmbhodher yo 'tyantam pāram āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who has completely reached the far shore of the ocean of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),

children.text: sa puṇyaguṇaratnāḍhyas tvadguṇārṇavapāragaḥ || NagAst_58
children.translated_text: rich in the jewels of merit and virtues — he has gone beyond the ocean of your qualities. || 58 ||

children.text: iti stutvā jagannātham acintyam anidarśanam |
children.translated_text: Thus having praised the Lord of the World (<s>Jagannātha</s>), who is inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>) and beyond indication (<s>anidarśana</s>),

children.text: yad avāptaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ tenāstu tvatsamaṃ jagat || NagAst_59
children.translated_text: by whatever merit has been obtained by me — by that, may the world become equal to you! || 59 ||

body.translated_text: || Thus the <s>Acintyastava</s> (Hymn to the Inconceivable) is complete. ||
